description: §19.8.3 handling form 2 (S451 R11) — a `?{}` query handled by a `match` on its result, as a declaration's right-hand side in a server function (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"). The function must be SERVER-placed and the query must run: `notes` has a row → `::Ok(row)`; `empties` is empty → `::Ok(not)`; `gone` is declared but never created, so the query fails to run → `::QueryFailed(m)` with the driver's message bound to `m`. Pre-S454 this compiled at exit 0 but SILENTLY moved each function to the CLIENT, where the query emitted as `null /* sql-ref unresolved */.get()` (route inference never saw the `?{}` in the `match` scrutinee).
rationale: §19.8.3: "**A `match` on the result** — the success value arrives as `::Ok` (§19.7.1)", with the example `const rows = match ?{…}.all() { ::Ok(found) :> found  ::QueryFailed(m) :> { log(m); [] }  _ :> [] }`. §18.3: "A `match` expression MAY appear as the right-hand side of a variable declaration or assignment". §19.8.3: a query that runs and matches nothing succeeds (`.get()` → `not`); only a query that fails to run produces a `SqlError` variant.
